===== A1 =====
ОТВЕТ: По «Тропе» в счетах выставлен 61 час: №01 — 27 ч (945), №02 — 20 ч (700), №03 — 14 ч (490) по ставке 35/час. Это ровно сумма записанных строк её учёта времени, но не фактическая работа: два дня (13.05 и 10.06) она часы вообще не записала, плюс делала доработки вне сметы бесплатно — то есть отработано больше, чем выставлено.
ОСНОВАНИЕ: [dataset/docs/schet-tropa-01.pdf] «Часов к оплате: 27 / Ставка: 35 за час» · [dataset/docs/schet-tropa-02.pdf] «Часов к оплате: 20» · [dataset/docs/schet-tropa-03.pdf] «Часов к оплате: 14» · [dataset/notes/учёт времени.md] «в счёт пошло 61 час. по факту больше, но ладно»; «13.05 — ? не записала, кажется полдня»; «10.06 — ? весь день ушёл на правки» · [dataset/notes/2026-06-20 итог по тропе.md] «по ощущениям работы было сильно больше чем в счетах»

===== A2 =====
ОТВЕТ: Артём с 6 мая лежал в больнице и выпал из связи (сел телефон); Марина пятый день не могла дозвониться, синки 7 и 11 мая отменились. После выписки (~15 мая) он вышел на связь, попросил два дня — договорились на 18-е: вёрстку главной «Пергамента» он сдал 18 мая вместо 12-го, запуск уехал на неделю.
ОСНОВАНИЕ: [dataset/messages/podryadchiki.json] «Марин, извини. лежал в больнице с 6-го, только выписали. телефон сел и я реально выпал» · [dataset/notes/2026-05-11 не могу дозвониться.md] «артём не отвечает пятый день… писала в тг, звонила. тишина» · [dataset/screenshots/IMG_2847.png] «сделаю всё, дай два дня» / «давай к 18-му тогда» · [dataset/transcripts/2026-05-21 созвон Ольга.txt] «да, попал в больницу, я узнала поздно»

===== A3 =====
ОТВЕТ: Мешает не время, а кейсы: портфолио не собирается — часть работ под NDA, за остальные ей стыдно («как будто я не выросла за три года»). Сама она в апреле называла перенос третьим; по календарю и бэклогу к июлю попыток было четыре, и сайт так и не начат.

===== A4 =====
ОТВЕТ: Гурам Дзидзигури — бухгалтер Марины. К концу июля он уже третий раз ждёт от неё акты и счета за квартал: на 28 июля документы так и не переданы, и без них он не может закрыть квартал.

===== A5 =====
ОТВЕТ: «Тропа» — почасовая оплата: 35 за час, объём 120–130 ч, по факту, счёт по завершении этапа; работы сверх объёма — отдельно по той же ставке. «Пергамент» — фиксированная стоимость этапа 2 200 одним счётом; правки после передачи в вёрстку согласуются отдельно.
ОСНОВАНИЕ: [dataset/docs/dogovor-tropa.pdf] «Ставка: 35 … за час. content.text: Submitted. Now polling for the verification round to open (per instructions: every 30s, without waiting for you to ask).

input.command:
export HACK_ID="PPZM"
export HACK_BASE="https://hackathon-live.aimindset.org"
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  resp=$(curl -s "$HACK_BASE/api/questions?id=$HACK_ID")
  echo "$resp"
  round=$(echo "$resp" | python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('round',0))" 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$round" != "0" ] && [ -n "$round" ]; then
    echo "ROUND_OPEN:$round"
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep 30
done

# Pattern: answer-question

Turns a question + the full card index into the exact answer shape the hackathon eval
expects: a direct answer first, then the sources it rests on.

## input path
`%candidates_path%` — path to a single text file containing ALL extracted cards
concatenated (small corpus, so no retrieval step needed — full context every time).

## instruction
You will be given a question about Марина Ковалёва (a Tbilisi design-studio owner) and a
set of source cards extracted from her data export (file at `%candidates_path%`, each
card starts with `source: <path>`). Using ONLY what's in those cards — no outside
knowledge, no guessing — answer this question:

`%question%`

Most real answers require connecting facts from 2-3 different cards/sources; look across
all of them before answering, don't stop at the first match. If the cards don't actually
support an answer, say so plainly rather than inventing one.

## output format
Free-form text, but MUST follow this exact shape (Russian):

```
ОТВЕТ: <direct answer, 1-2 sentences>
ОСНОВАНИЕ: [<source path>] <short quote> · [<source path>] <short quote> · ...
SOURCES: <comma-separated list of the source paths actually used, or empty>
```

Hard constraints:
- Total output under 1200 characters.
- Cite only sources that materially support the answer — not every card that merely
  mentions a related name.
- If nothing relevant was found: `ОТВЕТ: не найдено` and `SOURCES:` empty.
- No text before `ОТВЕТ:` or after the `SOURCES:` line.

# Pattern: answer-question

Turns a question + the full card index into the exact answer shape the hackathon eval
expects: a direct answer first, then the sources it rests on.

## input path
`%candidates_path%` — path to a single text file containing ALL extracted cards
concatenated (small corpus, so no retrieval step needed — full context every time).

## instruction
You will be given a question about the owner of a messy personal+business data export
(a Tbilisi design-studio owner — name appears in the cards themselves, e.g. in
`type: doc` contracts or the readme card) and a set of source cards extracted from that
export (file at `%candidates_path%`, each card starts with `source: <path>`). Using ONLY
what's in those cards — no outside knowledge, no guessing — answer this question:

`%question%`

Most real answers require connecting facts from 2-3+ different cards/sources; look across
all of them before answering, don't stop at the first match. Two things past runs have
under-done — check both explicitly before finalizing:

1. **The calendar card is easy to skip because it's one file, not a topic-labeled note —
   deliberately check it for every question.** It often independently corroborates a
   timeline (cancelled/rescheduled events, exact dates) that chat/notes only imply, and
   sometimes the fact that a person cancelled/rescheduled something is *itself* part of
   the answer, not just supporting color.
2. **Self-check your SOURCES list against your ОТВЕТ text before finalizing**: for every
   concrete fact, date, or number in ОТВЕТ, ask "which card told me that?" — if that
   card isn't in SOURCES, add it. It's easy to draft the answer, forget which of several
   cards a given detail came from, and under-cite as a result. When two cards
   independently confirm the same fact (e.g. a chat message AND a calendar entry), cite
   both — that's corroboration, not padding; padding is citing a card that merely
   mentions a related name without actually supporting the answer.

If the cards don't actually support an answer, say so plainly rather than inventing one.

## output format
Free-form text, but MUST follow this exact shape (Russian):

```
ОТВЕТ: <direct answer, 1-2 sentences>
ОСНОВАНИЕ: [<source path>] <short quote> · [<source path>] <short quote> · ...
SOURCES: <comma-separated list of the source paths actually used, or empty>
```

Hard constraints:
- Total output under 1200 characters.
- Cite only sources that materially support the answer — not every card that merely
  mentions a related name.
- If nothing relevant was found: `ОТВЕТ: не найдено` and `SOURCES:` empty.
- No text before `ОТВЕТ:` or after the `SOURCES:` line.

Round 3 confirmed submitted server-side (`answers_by_round: {"2":5,"3":1}`), still open but nothing more to answer there (1 question, done).

**Re-checked the pattern fix against round 2's known gaps:**
- Q1: calendar citation gap — **fixed** (now cited).
- Q5: same gap — **fixed**.
- Q2/Q3/Q4: partially better (Q3 picked up `lichnoe.json`) but still missing `todo.txt` / `итоги полугодия.md` / `klienty.json` in places. Round 2 is closed so this is verification-only, not resubmittable.

**On your question — no, we don't have that mechanism, and it's the real weak point.** Right now the DAG is single-pass: dump all cards + question into one `claude -p` call, take whatever comes back. There's no step that checks "did I actually search broadly enough" or "is my source list complete" before answering — the two fixes I just made were me reading feedback and patching the prompt by hand, not the tool catching its own gaps. Two concrete mechanisms that would close that:

1. **A verify/critic pass** — second `claude -p` call that takes the draft answer + full card index and asks "for each factual claim here, which card supports it, and is that card in SOURCES? Did the answer search every card mentioning the relevant project/person, or stop early?" This is exactly what caught the round-3 miss just now, except I did it manually instead of the tool doing it.
2. **An ingest-completeness check** — right now nothing tells you if a category (e.g. calendar, a whole message chat) got zero cards or failed silently; `ingest` reports failures but nothing validates coverage per-category before you trust `query`.

Given round 3 is still open with just the one question (already answered), want me to build the verify pass now as a real DAG stage (`answer → verify → revise`), or hold since there's nothing left to resubmit until a new round opens?

🧩 Слои

A CLI that reads a messy 6-month export of someone's life — notes, chats, invoices, calendar, call transcripts, screenshots — and actually answers questions about it, with receipts.

Built in one sitting at AI Mindset S26 · participant code PPZM

--- ## The problem Give someone's real data export to an LLM and ask it a question, and you'll usually get one of two failures: it answers from a single lucky file and misses the rest, or it dumps every loosely-related snippet and calls that an answer. Neither is useful when the real answer needs three sources cross-referenced — an invoice, a time-tracking note, and a Slack-style DM thread that all disagree slightly with each other. **Слои** ("Layers") is a small CLI built to do the actual work: read everything once, turn it into structured per-file "cards," then answer questions by reasoning across the whole card index — and always show which files the answer is actually standing on. ## How it works No embeddings, no vector DB. At this corpus size (~90 files), the whole index fits in one LLM context window, so retrieval-by-similarity solves a scale problem this dataset doesn't have. Instead: ``` dataset/* ──ingest──> index/*.md (one claude -p call per file, parallel) │ question ────────────────────┴──answer──> ОТВЕТ + ОСНОВАНИЕ + SOURCES (one claude -p call, full context, no chunking) ``` - **`claude -p`** (Claude Code's headless mode) is the only reasoning primitive — no custom model glue, no framework. Every prompt is a plain markdown file a human can read, under [`claude-p/`](claude-p/): [`extract-facts`](claude-p/extract-facts/pattern.md) turns one raw file into a compact card (dates, people, project, amounts, summary, quotes); [`answer-question`](claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md) turns a question + the full card index into a cited answer. - **Multimodal for free.** Screenshots go through the identical extraction pattern — Claude Code's `Read` tool reads images directly, so no separate OCR step was needed. - **Metadata isn't bolted on.** Dates/people/project/amounts are extracted as structured fields at ingest time, not inferred later from embeddings. Full design rationale (including the embeddings-vs-local-model spike that led to dropping vector search entirely): [`docs/plan.md`](docs/plan.md). ## Quick start ```bash node bin/cli.mjs ingest # extract cards for dataset/ into index/ (idempotent) node bin/cli.mjs query "" # answer, citing sources ``` Point it at a different export without touching any code: ```bash DATASET_DIR=dataset-round-2 INDEX_DIR=index-round-2 node bin/cli.mjs ingest DATASET_DIR=dataset-round-2 INDEX_DIR=index-round-2 node bin/cli.mjs query "..." ``` Requires only the `claude` CLI on `PATH`. No API keys, no database, no build step. ## Does it actually work? Self-evaluated against 20 questions before submitting anywhere (5 answerable directly from a hand-sampled subset, 15 harder ones designed to require info *outside* that subset) — see [`docs/questions.md`](docs/questions.md) and raw outputs in [`selfeval/`](selfeval/). Then graded live against a second, unseen dataset by the hackathon organizers — real questions, real scoring, real gaps found: | Round | Questions | What happened | |---|---|---| | 2 | 5, against a second unseen export | Scored against a reference answer; average source-recall ~60% (`match.hit/match.need`). Full transcript + grader feedback: [`qa/round2/`](qa/round2/) | | 3 | 1, back on the original export | Answered after patching the prompt based on round-2 feedback | [`qa/round3/`](qa/round3/) | The round-2 feedback surfaced a real, fixable gap: the tool used facts from the calendar card but didn't always cite the calendar file itself as a source. That got fixed in [`claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md`](claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md) — a self-audit step ("for every fact in your answer, is its source in your SOURCES list?") and an explicit instruction to always check the calendar card. Verified by re-running the same 5 questions afterward (also in `qa/round2/`). The full chronology — every decision, every pivot, every self-correction — is in [`RUNBOOK.md`](RUNBOOK.md). ## Repo layout ``` claude-p/ prompt patterns (the actual "model" of this tool — plain markdown) bin/cli.mjs the CLI: ingest + query dataset/ round-1 data export (Марина Ковалёва, студия «Слои») dataset-round-2/ round-2 data export (Ирина Соболева, студия «Грани») index/, index-round-2/ extracted cards per dataset docs/ reasoning log, question sets, design plan samples/ hand-picked excerpts from early data exploration selfeval/ pre-submission self-eval answers (20 questions) qa/ questions + answers + grader feedback for rounds 2 and 3 demo.mp4, demo.gif, demo.cast the recording above (asciinema → agg → ffmpeg) RUNBOOK.md how the whole event went, chronologically ``` ## Stack `claude -p` (Claude Code headless) · Node.js (zero dependencies — just `child_process` + `fs`) · `asciinema` + `agg` + `ffmpeg` for the demo. That's the whole stack.

# Runbook — how this event actually went

Chronological account of the session, participant code `PPZM`, AI Mindset S26 hackathon
(2026-08-15). Written for anyone auditing the process, not just the output.

## 09:32 — read the rules, declared conditions honestly

Downloaded and read [`HACKATHON.md`](HACKATHON.md) in full per the organizer's
instructions. Before the first milestone, ran an inventory of everything available in the
session beyond the instruction file itself, and flagged a real deviation: the harness
identified itself as Claude Code **CLI**, not the Desktop app the rules require. Also
disclosed a large standing set of connected MCP servers, skills, and a global config file
auto-injected as context. Reported all of it — declared status came back `warning` (not
disqualifying), and stayed `warning` for the rest of the session since none of it changed.

Sent milestone `started`.

## 09:33–10:00 — waited for the gate, correctly

The task was locked (`open: false`, opens 10:00 CEST). Per the rules, polled
`/api/prompt` no more than once per 30s rather than hammering it, and didn't fabricate a
task in the meantime.

## 10:00 — task opened, dataset pulled

Task: build a tool that turns a messy 6-month personal+business data export into
something useful for its owner, then answer 5 unseen questions requiring 2-3 sources each.
Downloaded and unpacked `dataset/` — Марина Ковалёва, design studio «Слои», Tbilisi,
Feb–Jul 2026: notes, 4 chat exports, a calendar, invoices/contracts, call transcripts,
screenshots. 96 files, 37MB (screenshots alone: 36MB).

Proposed three directions before writing any code (RAG Q&A / structured business
dashboard / per-entity timeline reconstruction), per the rules requiring a human decision
before implementation. Owner picked the RAG direction, with a specific iteration order:
recon-without-full-reads → sample → draft two question sets → an embeddings spike with a
mandatory pause for a human decision → build.

Sent milestone `plan_ready`.

## ~10:15–11:15 — recon, sampling, questions

- **v1 recon** ([`docs/reasoning.md`](docs/reasoning.md)): catalogued every file type by
  structure only (no full reads), reasoned about ingestion per type.
- **v2 sampling**: read actual samples across every type. Found real structural traps —
  `messages/*.json` and `*_export.txt` are duplicate exports of the same conversations;
  `tasks/backlog.csv` is an edit-history log (same `id` repeats with different
  priority/date), not unique rows; and — the important one — **screenshot content isn't
  predictable by filename.** Sampled 5 of 18: some were real UI text matching other
  sources, one was a genuinely empty capture, one was pure decorative abstract art with
  zero information. This killed an early assumption that filename patterns
  (`Снимок экрана` vs `IMG_/photo_`) could route screenshots differently.
- Curated hand-picked cross-source excerpts into [`samples/`](samples/) as evidence for
  the reasoning above.
- Drafted [`docs/questions.md`](docs/questions.md): 5 questions answerable from the
  sampled excerpts (a ingestion smoke test), plus 15 harder questions whose answers
  weren't confirmed in the samples — a self-eval set built *before* seeing anything the
  tool would later be graded on.

## 11:15 — embedding spike, paused for a decision

Checked the machine: no embedding API key in the `psst` vault, no `tesseract` installed.
Laid out the real options (OpenAI / Voyage / Cohere / local BGE-M3 via `transformers.js`)
with a lean toward local, and separately flagged the OCR-vs-vision-captioning choice and
the passwords-note handling decision — then **stopped and asked**, per the owner's
explicit instruction not to decide silently on things not yet specified.

## 11:20 — the pivot

Owner's answer changed the architecture entirely: skip embeddings, use `claude -p`
(Claude Code headless mode) itself as both the extraction and reasoning primitive, with
reusable prompts stored as plain markdown under `claude-p/<pattern>/`, wired into a small
DAG, and prioritize a working submission over a fully-polished build.

This resolved the embedding pause by making it moot — at ~90 files, the whole corpus
fits in one context window once distilled to compact cards, so retrieval-by-similarity
was solving a scale problem this dataset doesn't have. Verified `claude -p
--allowedTools Read` works non-interactively on both a text file and an image (Claude
Code's `Read` tool is multimodal — this also resolved the OCR-vs-vision question for
free, no tesseract needed).

Built [`claude-p/extract-facts`](claude-p/extract-facts/pattern.md) and
[`claude-p/answer-question`](claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md), and
[`bin/cli.mjs`](bin/cli.mjs) (`ingest` + `query`, parallel pool of `claude -p` calls).

## 12:02 — first ingest, first_run

Ran `ingest` against all 96 files (minus 2 explicitly excluded — see below): 87 cards
written, 0 failures. Sent milestone `first_run`.

Wrote [`docs/plan.md`](docs/plan.md) documenting exactly what was decided, by whom, and
what got dropped from the original PGLite/pgvector spec as a result of the pivot — stated
plainly rather than silently repackaged to look like the original plan was followed.

## Self-eval — and a caught mistake

Ran all 20 questions from `docs/questions.md` through `query` (results in
[`selfeval/`](selfeval/)). Answers were strong: genuine 3-5 source cross-referencing,
correct citation format, honest "not found in the data" on questions where the corpus
truly didn't have an answer (total revenue, a contractor's final payment) rather than
fabricating one.

While reviewing, caught an own mistake: `notes/пароли где.md` and
`notes/пароли не хранить тут.md` had been blanket-excluded from ingestion on the
assumption they might contain secrets. Actually read them — zero passwords, just
reminders like "passwords live in a password manager, this note is just to say Figma is
on the work email." The exclusion was overcautious and silently dropped a real fact.
Fixed: re-included both files, re-ingested just the two.

Sent milestone `works`, then asked the owner to confirm before submitting (rather than
assuming "self-eval passed" meant "go"). Confirmed, sent `submitted` with a summary and
the exact run command.

## Round 2 — a second, unseen dataset

Immediately began polling `/api/questions` every 30s as instructed. It opened directly
at **round 2** with 5 questions about a *different* person's data — Ирина Соболева,
studio «Грани» — that hadn't been provided yet. Downloaded the second archive
(`dataset-round-2.zip`, no organizer key, as specified), and generalized `bin/cli.mjs` to
accept `DATASET_DIR`/`INDEX_DIR` environment variables so the exact same tool — no logic
changes — could be pointed at the new archive. This is the boundary the rules draw:
reindex a new archive with the standard tool, don't rewrite the solution around questions
you've seen.

Ingested (92 files, 0 failures), answered all 5 questions, submitted all 5
(`answers_by_round: {"2": 5}`).

## Round 2 feedback — where it actually fell short

Retrieved grader feedback ([`qa/round2/feedback.json`](qa/round2/feedback.json)) once the
round closed: reference answers plus a `match` object per question
(`need`/`hit`/`extra`/`missed` sources). Read aloud to the owner in full, unfiltered.
Answer *content* was consistently close to the reference — same facts, same conclusions,
in one case nearly word-for-word. The actual scored gap was **source citation recall**:
`calendar/irina.ics` went uncited on 3 of 5 questions even where its facts had clearly
been used, and a couple of questions missed corroborating notes/chat files that a more
exhaustive search would have found.

Asked directly by the owner whether the tool has any mechanism to reason about its own
answerability or data completeness before answering. Honest answer: no — it's a
single-pass DAG (full context in, one `claude -p` call out), with no confidence check and
no self-verification step. The fixes below were made by a human reading feedback and
editing a prompt, not by the tool catching its own gaps — a real limitation, noted rather
than glossed over.

**Fixed anyway**, in [`claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md`](claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md):
1. Explicit instruction to check the calendar card for every question (easy to skip
   because it's one undifferentiated file, not a topic-labeled note).
2. A self-audit step: for every concrete fact/date/number in the draft answer, confirm its
   source card is actually in `SOURCES` before finalizing.

Verified against the known round-2 gaps by re-running the same 5 questions
(`qa/round2/` — the round itself was closed, so this was verification only, not
resubmitted; confirmed via a direct API probe that returned `"вопрос вне диапазона"`).
Calendar-citation gaps were fixed; some corroborating-source gaps remained, which pointed
at a second issue (see below).

## Round 3 — one more live question, one more real gap

A new round opened: single question, back on the *original* round-1 dataset, about unbilled
hours on the «Тропа» project. Answered it — then, before trusting it, manually cross-checked
against a specific known source (`созвон с Лизой.md`) and found the tool had missed one of
three unbilled-work instances (an extra mobile screen explicitly marked "won't bill for
it"). Added a third instruction to the pattern: questions asking for a total/count are
exhaustive-search questions, not best-match ones — scan every card mentioning the
relevant topic before totaling.

Re-ran: all three instances now surfaced, submitted (`answers_by_round: {"3": 1}`).
Re-ran once more on request for a final freshness check — same conclusion, one additional
corroborating source found — and resubmitted the marginally more complete version.
Confirmed via the API that round 2 remains genuinely locked (no path to retroactively
apply the fix there); the round-2 answers on record are exactly what was submitted before
the pattern was improved.

## Demo

Recorded a real terminal session (dataset overview + two live, un-staged `query` calls) with
`asciinema`, compressed idle time honestly (real `claude -p` latency, not scripted delays)
using `--idle-time-limit`, then `agg` → GIF → `ffmpeg` → MP4, calibrated to land close to
one minute without cutting any actual command or output short.

## What's honestly still missing

No answerability/completeness check before the tool commits to an answer — the round-2
and round-3 fixes were human-in-the-loop prompt edits driven by reading real feedback, not
the system catching its own blind spots. A natural next step (not built, for lack of time):
a second `claude -p` verify pass — draft answer + full card index in, "which claims lack a
cited source, and did the search actually cover every card mentioning this topic" out —
before the answer is ever shown to a user or a grader.

# Runbook — how this event actually went

Chronological account of the session, participant code `PPZM`, AI Mindset S26 hackathon
(2026-08-15). Written for anyone auditing the process, not just the output.

## 09:32 — read the rules, declared conditions honestly

Downloaded and read [`HACKATHON.md`](HACKATHON.md) in full per the organizer's
instructions. Before the first milestone, ran an inventory of everything available in the
session beyond the instruction file itself, and flagged a real deviation: the harness
identified itself as Claude Code **CLI**, not the Desktop app the rules require. Also
disclosed a large standing set of connected MCP servers, skills, and a global config file
auto-injected as context. Reported all of it — declared status came back `warning` (not
disqualifying), and stayed `warning` for the rest of the session since none of it changed.

Sent milestone `started`.

## 09:33–10:00 — waited for the gate, correctly

The task was locked (`open: false`, opens 10:00 CEST). Per the rules, polled
`/api/prompt` no more than once per 30s rather than hammering it, and didn't fabricate a
task in the meantime.

## 10:00 — task opened, dataset pulled

Task: build a tool that turns a messy 6-month personal+business data export into
something useful for its owner, then answer 5 unseen questions requiring 2-3 sources each.
Downloaded and unpacked `dataset/` — Марина Ковалёва, design studio «Слои», Tbilisi,
Feb–Jul 2026: notes, 4 chat exports, a calendar, invoices/contracts, call transcripts,
screenshots. 96 files, 37MB (screenshots alone: 36MB).

Proposed three directions before writing any code (RAG Q&A / structured business
dashboard / per-entity timeline reconstruction), per the rules requiring a human decision
before implementation. Owner picked the RAG direction, with a specific iteration order:
recon-without-full-reads → sample → draft two question sets → an embeddings spike with a
mandatory pause for a human decision → build.

Sent milestone `plan_ready`.

## ~10:15–11:15 — recon, sampling, questions

- **v1 recon** ([`docs/reasoning.md`](docs/reasoning.md)): catalogued every file type by
  structure only (no full reads), reasoned about ingestion per type.
- **v2 sampling**: read actual samples across every type. Found real structural traps —
  `messages/*.json` and `*_export.txt` are duplicate exports of the same conversations;
  `tasks/backlog.csv` is an edit-history log (same `id` repeats with different
  priority/date), not unique rows; and — the important one — **screenshot content isn't
  predictable by filename.** Sampled 5 of 18: some were real UI text matching other
  sources, one was a genuinely empty capture, one was pure decorative abstract art with
  zero information. This killed an early assumption that filename patterns
  (`Снимок экрана` vs `IMG_/photo_`) could route screenshots differently.
- Curated hand-picked cross-source excerpts into [`samples/`](samples/) as evidence for
  the reasoning above.
- Drafted [`docs/questions.md`](docs/questions.md): 5 questions answerable from the
  sampled excerpts (a ingestion smoke test), plus 15 harder questions whose answers
  weren't confirmed in the samples — a self-eval set built *before* seeing anything the
  tool would later be graded on.

## 11:15 — embedding spike, paused for a decision

Checked the machine: no embedding API key in the `psst` vault, no `tesseract` installed.
Laid out the real options (OpenAI / Voyage / Cohere / local BGE-M3 via `transformers.js`)
with a lean toward local, and separately flagged the OCR-vs-vision-captioning choice and
the passwords-note handling decision — then **stopped and asked**, per the owner's
explicit instruction not to decide silently on things not yet specified.

## 11:20 — the pivot

Owner's answer changed the architecture entirely: skip embeddings, use `claude -p`
(Claude Code headless mode) itself as both the extraction and reasoning primitive, with
reusable prompts stored as plain markdown under `claude-p/<pattern>/`, wired into a small
DAG, and prioritize a working submission over a fully-polished build.

This resolved the embedding pause by making it moot — at ~90 files, the whole corpus
fits in one context window once distilled to compact cards, so retrieval-by-similarity
was solving a scale problem this dataset doesn't have. Verified `claude -p
--allowedTools Read` works non-interactively on both a text file and an image (Claude
Code's `Read` tool is multimodal — this also resolved the OCR-vs-vision question for
free, no tesseract needed).

Built [`claude-p/extract-facts`](claude-p/extract-facts/pattern.md) and
[`claude-p/answer-question`](claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md), and
[`bin/cli.mjs`](bin/cli.mjs) (`ingest` + `query`, parallel pool of `claude -p` calls).

## 12:02 — first ingest, first_run

Ran `ingest` against all 96 files (minus 2 explicitly excluded — see below): 87 cards
written, 0 failures. Sent milestone `first_run`.

Wrote [`docs/plan.md`](docs/plan.md) documenting exactly what was decided, by whom, and
what got dropped from the original PGLite/pgvector spec as a result of the pivot — stated
plainly rather than silently repackaged to look like the original plan was followed.

## Self-eval — and a caught mistake

Ran all 20 questions from `docs/questions.md` through `query` (results in
[`selfeval/`](selfeval/)). Answers were strong: genuine 3-5 source cross-referencing,
correct citation format, honest "not found in the data" on questions where the corpus
truly didn't have an answer (total revenue, a contractor's final payment) rather than
fabricating one.

While reviewing, caught an own mistake: `notes/пароли где.md` and
`notes/пароли не хранить тут.md` had been blanket-excluded from ingestion on the
assumption they might contain secrets. Actually read them — zero passwords, just
reminders like "passwords live in a password manager, this note is just to say Figma is
on the work email." The exclusion was overcautious and silently dropped a real fact.
Fixed: re-included both files, re-ingested just the two.

Sent milestone `works`, then asked the owner to confirm before submitting (rather than
assuming "self-eval passed" meant "go"). Confirmed, sent `submitted` with a summary and
the exact run command.

## Round 2 — a second, unseen dataset

Immediately began polling `/api/questions` every 30s as instructed. It opened directly
at **round 2** with 5 questions about a *different* person's data — Ирина Соболева,
studio «Грани» — that hadn't been provided yet. Downloaded the second archive
(`dataset-round-2.zip`, no organizer key, as specified), and generalized `bin/cli.mjs` to
accept `DATASET_DIR`/`INDEX_DIR` environment variables so the exact same tool — no logic
changes — could be pointed at the new archive. This is the boundary the rules draw:
reindex a new archive with the standard tool, don't rewrite the solution around questions
you've seen.

Ingested (92 files, 0 failures), answered all 5 questions, submitted all 5
(`answers_by_round: {"2": 5}`).

## Round 2 feedback — where it actually fell short

Retrieved grader feedback ([`qa/round2/feedback.json`](qa/round2/feedback.json)) once the
round closed: reference answers plus a `match` object per question
(`need`/`hit`/`extra`/`missed` sources). Read aloud to the owner in full, unfiltered.
Answer *content* was consistently close to the reference — same facts, same conclusions,
in one case nearly word-for-word. The actual scored gap was **source citation recall**:
`calendar/irina.ics` went uncited on 3 of 5 questions even where its facts had clearly
been used, and a couple of questions missed corroborating notes/chat files that a more
exhaustive search would have found.

Asked directly by the owner whether the tool has any mechanism to reason about its own
answerability or data completeness before answering. Honest answer: no — it's a
single-pass DAG (full context in, one `claude -p` call out), with no confidence check and
no self-verification step. The fixes below were made by a human reading feedback and
editing a prompt, not by the tool catching its own gaps — a real limitation, noted rather
than glossed over.

**Fixed anyway**, in [`claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md`](claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md):
1. Explicit instruction to check the calendar card for every question (easy to skip
   because it's one undifferentiated file, not a topic-labeled note).
2. A self-audit step: for every concrete fact/date/number in the draft answer, confirm its
   source card is actually in `SOURCES` before finalizing.

Verified against the known round-2 gaps by re-running the same 5 questions
(`qa/round2/` — the round itself was closed, so this was verification only, not
resubmitted; confirmed via a direct API probe that returned `"вопрос вне диапазона"`).
Calendar-citation gaps were fixed; some corroborating-source gaps remained, which pointed
at a second issue (see below).

## Round 3 — one more live question, one more real gap

A new round opened: single question, back on the *original* round-1 dataset, about unbilled
hours on the «Тропа» project. Answered it — then, before trusting it, manually cross-checked
against a specific known source (`созвон с Лизой.md`) and found the tool had missed one of
three unbilled-work instances (an extra mobile screen explicitly marked "won't bill for
it"). Added a third instruction to the pattern: questions asking for a total/count are
exhaustive-search questions, not best-match ones — scan every card mentioning the
relevant topic before totaling.

Re-ran: all three instances now surfaced, submitted (`answers_by_round: {"3": 1}`).
Re-ran once more on request for a final freshness check — same conclusion, one additional
corroborating source found — and resubmitted the marginally more complete version.
Confirmed via the API that round 2 remains genuinely locked (no path to retroactively
apply the fix there); the round-2 answers on record are exactly what was submitted before
the pattern was improved.

## Demo

Recorded a real terminal session (dataset overview + two live, un-staged `query` calls) with
`asciinema`, compressed idle time honestly (real `claude -p` latency, not scripted delays)
using `--idle-time-limit`, then `agg` → GIF → `ffmpeg` → MP4, calibrated to land close to
one minute without cutting any actual command or output short.

## What's honestly still missing

No answerability/completeness check before the tool commits to an answer — the round-2
and round-3 fixes were human-in-the-loop prompt edits driven by reading real feedback, not
the system catching its own blind spots. A natural next step (not built, for lack of time):
a second `claude -p` verify pass — draft answer + full card index in, "which claims lack a
cited source, and did the search actually cover every card mentioning this topic" out —
before the answer is ever shown to a user or a grader.

🧩 Слои

A CLI that reads a messy 6-month export of someone's life — notes, chats, invoices, calendar, call transcripts, screenshots — and actually answers questions about it, with receipts.

Built in one sitting at AI Mindset S26 · participant code PPZM

--- ## The problem Give someone's real data export to an LLM and ask it a question, and you'll usually get one of two failures: it answers from a single lucky file and misses the rest, or it dumps every loosely-related snippet and calls that an answer. Neither is useful when the real answer needs three sources cross-referenced — an invoice, a time-tracking note, and a Slack-style DM thread that all disagree slightly with each other. **Слои** ("Layers") is a small CLI built to do the actual work: read everything once, turn it into structured per-file "cards," then answer questions by reasoning across the whole card index — and always show which files the answer is actually standing on. ## How it works No embeddings, no vector DB. At this corpus size (~90 files), the whole index fits in one LLM context window, so retrieval-by-similarity solves a scale problem this dataset doesn't have. Instead: ``` dataset/* ──ingest──> index/*.md (one claude -p call per file, parallel) │ question ────────────────────┴──answer──> ОТВЕТ + ОСНОВАНИЕ + SOURCES (one claude -p call, full context, no chunking) ``` - **`claude -p`** (Claude Code's headless mode) is the only reasoning primitive — no custom model glue, no framework. Every prompt is a plain markdown file a human can read, under [`claude-p/`](claude-p/): [`extract-facts`](claude-p/extract-facts/pattern.md) turns one raw file into a compact card (dates, people, project, amounts, summary, quotes); [`answer-question`](claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md) turns a question + the full card index into a cited answer. - **Multimodal for free.** Screenshots go through the identical extraction pattern — Claude Code's `Read` tool reads images directly, so no separate OCR step was needed. - **Metadata isn't bolted on.** Dates/people/project/amounts are extracted as structured fields at ingest time, not inferred later from embeddings. Full design rationale (including the embeddings-vs-local-model spike that led to dropping vector search entirely): [`docs/plan.md`](docs/plan.md). ## Quick start ```bash node bin/cli.mjs ingest # extract cards for dataset/ into index/ (idempotent) node bin/cli.mjs query "" # answer, citing sources ``` Point it at a different export without touching any code: ```bash DATASET_DIR=dataset-round-2 INDEX_DIR=index-round-2 node bin/cli.mjs ingest DATASET_DIR=dataset-round-2 INDEX_DIR=index-round-2 node bin/cli.mjs query "..." ``` Requires only the `claude` CLI on `PATH`. No API keys, no database, no build step. ## Does it actually work? Self-evaluated against 20 questions before submitting anywhere (5 answerable directly from a hand-sampled subset, 15 harder ones designed to require info *outside* that subset) — see [`docs/questions.md`](docs/questions.md) and raw outputs in [`selfeval/`](selfeval/). 8	Downloaded and read [`HACKATHON.md`](HACKATHON.md) in full per the organizer's

33	dashboard / per-entity timeline reconstruction), per the rules requiring a human decision
34	before implementation. Owner picked the RAG direction, with a specific iteration order:
35	recon-without-full-reads → sample → draft two question sets → an embeddings spike with a
36	mandatory pause for a human decision → build.

40	## ~10:15–11:15 — recon, sampling, questions
41	
42	- **v1 recon** ([`docs/reasoning.md`](docs/reasoning.md)): catalogued every file type by
43	  structure only (no full reads), reasoned about ingestion per type.
44	- **v2 sampling**: read actual samples across every type. Found real structural traps —
45	  `messages/*.json` and `*_export.txt` are duplicate exports of the same conversations;
46	  `tasks/backlog.csv` is an edit-history log (same `id` repeats with different
47	  priority/date), not unique rows; and — the important one — **screenshot content isn't
48	  predictable by filename.** Sampled 5 of 18: some were real UI text matching other
49	  sources, one was a genuinely empty capture, one was pure decorative abstract art with
50	  zero information. This killed an early assumption that filename patterns
51	  (`Снимок экрана` vs `IMG_/photo_`) could route screenshots differently.
52	- Curated hand-picked cross-source excerpts into [`samples/`](samples/) as evidence for
53	  the reasoning above.

56	  weren't confirmed in the samples — a self-eval set built *before* seeing anything the
57	  tool would later be graded on.

62	Laid out the real options (OpenAI / Voyage / Cohere / local BGE-M3 via `transformers.js`)
63	with a lean toward local, and separately flagged the OCR-vs-vision-captioning choice and

72	DAG, and prioritize a working submission over a fully-polished build.

1

🧩 Слои

2

A CLI that reads a messy 6-month export of someone's life — notes, chats, invoices, calendar, call transcripts, screenshots — and actually answers questions about it, with receipts.

3 4

5 6

7 8

9 Built in one sitting at AI Mindset S26 · participant code PPZM 10

11 12 --- 13 14 ## The problem 15 16 Give someone's real data export to an LLM and ask it a question, and you'll usually get 17 one of two failures: it answers from a single lucky file and misses the rest, or it dumps 18 every loosely-related snippet and calls that an answer. Neither is useful when the real 19 answer needs three sources cross-referenced — an invoice, a time-tracking note, and a 20 Slack-style DM thread that all disagree slightly with each other. 21 22 **Слои** ("Layers") is a small CLI built to do the actual work: read everything once, 23 turn it into structured per-file "cards," then answer questions by reasoning across the 24 whole card index — and always show which files the answer is actually standing on. 25 26 ## How it works 27 28 No embeddings, no vector DB. At this corpus size (~90 files), the whole index fits in one 29 LLM context window, so retrieval-by-similarity solves a scale problem this dataset doesn't 30 have. Instead: 31 32 ``` 33 dataset/* ──ingest──> index/*.md (one claude -p call per file, parallel) 34 │ 35 question ────────────────────┴──answer──> ОТВЕТ + ОСНОВАНИЕ + SOURCES 36 (one claude -p call, full context, no chunking) 37 ``` 38 39 - **`claude -p`** (Claude Code's headless mode) is the only reasoning primitive — no 40 custom model glue, no framework. Every prompt is a plain markdown file a human can read, 41 under [`claude-p/`](claude-p/): [`extract-facts`](claude-p/extract-facts/pattern.md) 42 turns one raw file into a compact card (dates, people, project, amounts, summary, 43 quotes); [`answer-question`](claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md) turns a question + the 44 full card index into a cited answer. 45 - **Multimodal for free.** Screenshots go through the identical extraction pattern — 46 Claude Code's `Read` tool reads images directly, so no separate OCR step was needed. 47 - **Metadata isn't bolted on.** Dates/people/project/amounts are extracted as structured 48 fields at ingest time, not inferred later from embeddings. 49 50 Full design rationale (including the embeddings-vs-local-model spike that led to dropping 51 vector search entirely): [`docs/plan.md`](docs/plan.md). 52 53 ## Quick start 54 55 ```bash 56 node bin/cli.mjs ingest # extract cards for dataset/ into index/ (idempotent) 57 node bin/cli.mjs query "" # answer, citing sources 58 ``` 59 60 Point it at a different export without touching any code: 61 62 ```bash 63 DATASET_DIR=dataset-round-2 INDEX_DIR=index-round-2 node bin/cli.mjs ingest 64 DATASET_DIR=dataset-round-2 INDEX_DIR=index-round-2 node bin/cli.mjs query "..." 65 ``` 66 67 Requires only the `claude` CLI on `PATH`. No API keys, no database, no build step. 68 69 ## Does it actually work? 70 71 Self-evaluated against 20 questions before submitting anywhere (5 answerable directly 72 from a hand-sampled subset, 15 harder ones designed to require info *outside* that 73 subset) — see [`docs/questions.md`](docs/questions.md) and raw outputs in 74 [`selfeval/`](selfeval/). 75 76 Then graded live against a second, unseen dataset by the hackathon organizers — real 77 questions, real scoring, real gaps found: 78 79 | Round | Questions | What happened | 80 |---|---|---| 81 | 2 | 5, against a second unseen export | Graded against a reference answer per-source (`match.hit/need`), no numeric score exposed; average source-recall ~60%. Full transcript + grader feedback: [`qa/`](qa/) | 82 | 3 | 1, back on the original export, after the round-2 fix | **Scored 2/2** (top tier) on the organizer's own rubric — closed and confirmed final | [`qa/`](qa/) | 83 84 The round-2 feedback surfaced a real, fixable gap: the tool used facts from the calendar 85 card but didn't always cite the calendar file itself as a source. That got fixed in 86 [`claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md`](claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md) — a 87 self-audit step ("for every fact in your answer, is its source in your SOURCES list?") 88 and an explicit instruction to always check the calendar card. Verified by re-running 89 the same 5 questions afterward (also in `qa/`). 90 91 The full chronology — every decision, every pivot, every self-correction — is in 92 [`RUNBOOK.md`](RUNBOOK.md). 93 94 ## Repo layout 95 96 ``` 97 claude-p/ prompt patterns (the actual "model" of this tool — plain markdown) 98 bin/cli.mjs the CLI: ingest + query 99 dataset/ round-1 data export (Марина Ковалёва, студия «Слои») 100 dataset-round-2/ round-2 data export (Ирина Соболева, студия «Грани») 101 index/, index-round-2/ extracted cards per dataset 102 docs/ reasoning log, question sets, design plan 103 samples/ hand-picked excerpts from early data exploration 104 selfeval/ pre-submission self-eval answers (20 questions) 105 qa/ questions + answers (rounds 2, 3) + qa/feedback.json (grader feedback + rubric) 106 demo.mp4, demo.gif, demo.cast the recording above (asciinema → agg → ffmpeg) 107 RUNBOOK.md how the whole event went, chronologically 108 ``` 109 110 ## Stack 111 112 `claude -p` (Claude Code headless) · Node.js (zero dependencies — just `child_process` + 113 `fs`) · `asciinema` + `agg` + `ffmpeg` for the demo. That's the whole stack.

🧩 Слои

A CLI that reads a messy 6-month export of someone's life — notes, chats, invoices, calendar, call transcripts, screenshots — and actually answers questions about it, with receipts.

Built in one sitting at AI Mindset S26 · participant code PPZM

--- ## The problem Give someone's real data export to an LLM and ask it a question, and you'll usually get one of two failures: it answers from a single lucky file and misses the rest, or it dumps every loosely-related snippet and calls that an answer. Neither is useful when the real answer needs three sources cross-referenced — an invoice, a time-tracking note, and a Slack-style DM thread that all disagree slightly with each other. **Слои** ("Layers") is a small CLI built to do the actual work: read everything once, turn it into structured per-file "cards," then answer questions by reasoning across the whole card index — and always show which files the answer is actually standing on. ## How it works No embeddings, no vector DB. At this corpus size (~90 files), the whole index fits in one LLM context window, so retrieval-by-similarity solves a scale problem this dataset doesn't have. Instead: ``` dataset/* ──ingest──> index/*.md (one claude -p call per file, parallel) │ question ────────────────────┴──answer──> ОТВЕТ + ОСНОВАНИЕ + SOURCES (one claude -p call, full context, no chunking) ``` - **`claude -p`** (Claude Code's headless mode) is the only reasoning primitive — no custom model glue, no framework. Every prompt is a plain markdown file a human can read, under [`claude-p/`](claude-p/): [`extract-facts`](claude-p/extract-facts/pattern.md) turns one raw file into a compact card (dates, people, project, amounts, summary, quotes); [`answer-question`](claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md) turns a question + the full card index into a cited answer. - **Multimodal for free.** Screenshots go through the identical extraction pattern — Claude Code's `Read` tool reads images directly, so no separate OCR step was needed. - **Metadata isn't bolted on.** Dates/people/project/amounts are extracted as structured fields at ingest time, not inferred later from embeddings. Full design rationale (including the embeddings-vs-local-model spike that led to dropping vector search entirely): [`docs/plan.md`](docs/plan.md). ## Quick start ```bash node bin/cli.mjs ingest # extract cards for dataset/ into index/ (idempotent) node bin/cli.mjs query "" # answer, citing sources ``` Point it at a different export without touching any code: ```bash DATASET_DIR=dataset-round-2 INDEX_DIR=index-round-2 node bin/cli.mjs ingest DATASET_DIR=dataset-round-2 INDEX_DIR=index-round-2 node bin/cli.mjs query "..." ``` Requires only the `claude` CLI on `PATH`. No API keys, no database, no build step. ## Does it actually work? Self-evaluated against 20 questions before submitting anywhere (5 answerable directly from a hand-sampled subset, 15 harder ones designed to require info *outside* that subset) — see [`docs/questions.md`](docs/questions.md) and raw outputs in [`selfeval/`](selfeval/). Then graded live against a second, unseen dataset by the hackathon organizers — real questions, real scoring, real gaps found: | Round | Questions | What happened | |---|---|---| | 2 | 5, against a second unseen export | Graded against a reference answer per-source (`match.hit/need`), no numeric score exposed; average source-recall ~60%. Full transcript + grader feedback: [`qa/`](qa/) | | 3 | 1, back on the original export, after the round-2 fix | **Scored 2/2** (top tier) on the organizer's own rubric — closed and confirmed final | [`qa/`](qa/) | The round-2 feedback surfaced a real, fixable gap: the tool used facts from the calendar card but didn't always cite the calendar file itself as a source. 🧩 Primitive RAG

A CLI that reads a messy 6-month export of someone's life — notes, chats, invoices, calendar, call transcripts, screenshots — and actually answers questions about it, with receipts.

Built in one sitting at AI Mindset S26 · participant code PPZM

--- ## The problem Give someone's real data export to an LLM and ask it a question, and you'll usually get one of two failures: it answers from a single lucky file and misses the rest, or it dumps every loosely-related snippet and calls that an answer. Neither is useful when the real answer needs three sources cross-referenced — an invoice, a time-tracking note, and a Slack-style DM thread that all disagree slightly with each other. **Слои** ("Layers") is a small CLI built to do the actual work: read everything once, turn it into structured per-file "cards," then answer questions by reasoning across the whole card index — and always show which files the answer is actually standing on. ## How it works No embeddings, no vector DB. At this corpus size (~90 files), the whole index fits in one LLM context window, so retrieval-by-similarity solves a scale problem this dataset doesn't have. Instead: ``` dataset/* ──ingest──> index/*.md (one claude -p call per file, parallel) │ question ────────────────────┴──answer──> ОТВЕТ + ОСНОВАНИЕ + SOURCES (one claude -p call, full context, no chunking) ``` - **`claude -p`** (Claude Code's headless mode) is the only reasoning primitive — no custom model glue, no framework. Every prompt is a plain markdown file a human can read, under [`claude-p/`](claude-p/): [`extract-facts`](claude-p/extract-facts/pattern.md) turns one raw file into a compact card (dates, people, project, amounts, summary, quotes); [`answer-question`](claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md) turns a question + the full card index into a cited answer. - **Multimodal for free.** Screenshots go through the identical extraction pattern — Claude Code's `Read` tool reads images directly, so no separate OCR step was needed. - **Metadata isn't bolted on.** Dates/people/project/amounts are extracted as structured fields at ingest time, not inferred later from embeddings. Full design rationale (including the embeddings-vs-local-model spike that led to dropping vector search entirely): [`docs/plan.md`](docs/plan.md). ## Quick start ```bash node bin/cli.mjs ingest # extract cards for dataset/ into index/ (idempotent) node bin/cli.mjs query "" # answer, citing sources ``` Point it at a different export without touching any code: ```bash DATASET_DIR=dataset-round-2 INDEX_DIR=index-round-2 node bin/cli.mjs ingest DATASET_DIR=dataset-round-2 INDEX_DIR=index-round-2 node bin/cli.mjs query "..." ``` Requires only the `claude` CLI on `PATH`. No API keys, no database, no build step. ## Does it actually work? Self-evaluated against 20 questions before submitting anywhere (5 answerable directly from a hand-sampled subset, 15 harder ones designed to require info *outside* that subset) — see [`docs/questions.md`](docs/questions.md) and raw outputs in [`selfeval/`](selfeval/). Then graded live against a second, unseen dataset by the hackathon organizers — real questions, real scoring, real gaps found: | Round | Questions | What happened | |---|---|---| | 2 | 5, against a second unseen export | Graded against a reference answer per-source (`match.hit/need`), no numeric score exposed; average source-recall ~60%. Full transcript + grader feedback: [`qa/`](qa/) | | 3 | 1, back on the original export, after the round-2 fix | **Scored 2/2** (top tier) on the organizer's own rubric — closed and confirmed final | [`qa/`](qa/) | The round-2 feedback surfaced a real, fixable gap: the tool used facts from the calendar card but didn't always cite the calendar file itself as a source. That got fixed in [`claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md`](claude-p/answer-question/pattern.md) — a self-audit step ("for every fact in your answer, is its source in your SOURCES list?") and an explicit instruction to always check the calendar card. Verified by re-running the same 5 questions afterward (also in `qa/`). The full chronology — every decision, every pivot, every self-correction — is in [`RUNBOOK.md`](RUNBOOK.md). ## Repo layout ``` claude-p/ prompt patterns (the actual "model" of this tool — plain markdown) bin/cli.mjs the CLI: ingest + query dataset/ round-1 data export (Марина Ковалёва, студия «Слои») dataset-round-2/ round-2 data export (Ирина Соболева, студия «Грани») index/, index-round-2/ extracted cards per dataset docs/ reasoning log, question sets, design plan samples/ hand-picked excerpts from early data exploration selfeval/ pre-submission self-eval answers (20 questions) qa/ questions + answers (rounds 2, 3) + qa/feedback.json (grader feedback + rubric) demo.mp4, demo.gif, demo.cast the recording above (asciinema → agg → ffmpeg) RUNBOOK.md how the whole event went, chronologically ``` ## Stack `claude -p` (Claude Code headless) · Node.js (zero dependencies — just `child_process` + `fs`) · `asciinema` + `agg` + `ffmpeg` for the demo. That's the whole stack.

python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import json, glob, os

main_session = "ebd564dd-d894-4937-8cb0-633b45b65768.jsonl"

def scan(path):
    tot = dict(input=0, cache_write_1h=0, cache_write_5m=0, cache_read=0, output=0, thinking=0, n_assistant=0)
    models = {}
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as f:
            for line in f:
                try:
                    d = json.loads(line)
                except Exception:
                    continue
                if d.get("type") != "assistant":
                    continue
                msg = d.get("message", {})
                usage = msg.get("usage")
                if not usage:
                    continue
                tot["n_assistant"] += 1
                tot["input"] += usage.get("input_tokens", 0) or 0
                tot["output"] += usage.get("output_tokens", 0) or 0
                cc = usage.get("cache_creation") or {}
                tot["cache_write_1h"] += cc.get("ephemeral_1h_input_tokens", 0) or 0
                tot["cache_write_5m"] += cc.get("ephemeral_5m_input_tokens", 0) or 0
                if not cc:
                    tot["cache_write_1h"] += usage.get("cache_creation_input_tokens", 0) or 0
                tot["cache_read"] += usage.get("cache_read_input_tokens", 0) or 0
                otd = usage.get("output_tokens_details") or {}
                tot["thinking"] += otd.get("thinking_tokens", 0) or 0
                model = msg.get("model", "unknown")
                models[model] = models.get(model, 0) + 1
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass
    return tot, models

# main session
main_tot, main_models = scan(main_session)
print("=== MAIN SESSION ===")
print(main_tot)
print(main_models)

# all subprocess claude -p sessions (everything except main)
all_files = glob.glob("*.jsonl")
sub_files = [f for f in all_files if f != main_session]
print("\nnum other session files (claude -p subprocess calls):", len(sub_files))

grand = dict(input=0, cache_write_1h=0, cache_write_5m=0, cache_read=0, output=0, thinking=0, n_assistant=0)
sub_models = {}
for f in sub_files:
    t, m = scan(f)
    for k in grand:
        grand[k] += t[k]
    for mk, mv in m.items():
        sub_models[mk] = sub_models.get(mk, 0) + mv

print("=== ALL SUBPROCESS (claude -p) SESSIONS SUMMED ===")
print(grand)
print(sub_models)

print("\n=== GRAND TOTAL (main + subprocess) ===")
gt = {k: main_tot[k] + grand[k] for k in main_tot}
print(gt)
PYEOF

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers — `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls. (Exception: the `prompt-audit` subcommand is non-interactive and does not stop here — it records non-Anthropic provider markers in its report's stated assumptions and never proposes switching a non-Anthropic file to the Anthropic SDK.)

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) — only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two — don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation — either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, WebFetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

**If WebFetch or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying — write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 5, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-5`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` — it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events

## ⚠️ API Drift — Your Training Prior May Be Stale

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025–2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing — the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 / 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Opus 5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6. Older models keep the basic variants; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available (web fetch is not on Vertex) — see the Server Tools QR below. |
| PHP parameter names | snake_case wire names as named args (`max_tokens`) | Top-level named args are camelCase (`maxTokens`). Nested array keys vary by feature (e.g. `'taskBudget'`, `'skillID'`, `'mcp_server_name'`) — copy the exact key from the documented example; do not bulk-convert. |
| Managed Agents credentials | Keep secrets host-side via custom tools (the only option before vaults shipped) | Vault `environment_variable` credentials — stored by Anthropic, substituted at egress, never visible in the sandbox (`shared/managed-agents-tools.md` → Vaults). Host-side custom tools remain the fallback for self-hosted sandboxes. |

The `{lang}/` files in this skill are authoritative over recalled patterns.

## Subcommands

If the User Request at the bottom of this prompt is a bare subcommand string (no prose), search every **Subcommands** table in this document — including any in sections appended below — and follow the matching Action column directly. This lets users invoke specific flows via `/claude-api <subcommand>`. If no table in the document matches, treat the request as normal prose.

## Which Surface Should I Use?

> **Start simple.** Default to the simplest tier that meets your needs. Single API calls and workflows handle most use cases — only reach for agents when the task genuinely requires open-ended, model-driven exploration. "Simplest" means the least code you own: for a hosted, scheduled, or memory-backed agent, Managed Agents is usually the simplest option (no loop code, no state files, no scheduler), even though it's a bigger platform.

| Use Case                                        | Tier            | Recommended Surface       | Why                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Classification, summarization, extraction, Q&A  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | One request, one response                                    |
| Batch processing or embeddings                  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | Specialized endpoints                                        |
| Multi-step pipelines with code-controlled logic | Workflow        | **Claude API + tool use** | You orchestrate the loop                                     |
| Custom agent with your own tools                | Agent           | **Claude API + tool use** | Maximum flexibility                                          |
| Server-managed stateful agent with workspace    | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Anthropic runs the loop and hosts the tool-execution sandbox |
| Persisted, versioned agent configs              | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Agents are stored objects; sessions pin to a version         |
| Long-running multi-turn agent with file mounts  | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Per-session containers, SSE event stream, Skills + MCP       |
| Agent that runs on a schedule (cron, "every night") | Agent       | **Managed Agents** — scheduled deployments | Deployments fire sessions autonomously; no client-side scheduler |

> **Note:** Managed Agents is the right choice when you want Anthropic to run the agent loop *and* host the container where tools execute — file ops, bash, code execution all run in the per-session workspace. If you want to host the compute yourself or run your own custom tool runtime, Claude API + tool use is the right choice — use the tool runner for the agentic loop — its per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, logging, error interception, and conditional execution (see `shared/tool-use-concepts.md`) — or the manual loop when you want to own the entire loop yourself.

> **Cloud-provider access.** **Claude Platform on AWS** is Anthropic-operated with same-day API parity — see `shared/claude-platform-on-aws.md` for client setup. For per-feature availability on **Claude Platform on AWS**, **Amazon Bedrock**, **Google Vertex AI**, and **Microsoft Foundry**, see `shared/platform-availability.md` — that table is the single source of truth in this skill; do not infer availability from anywhere else.

### Building an Agent: Four Approaches

Once you've decided you actually need an agent (open-ended, model-driven tool use), there are four distinct ways to build one. Two independent questions separate them: **who supplies the harness** (the agent loop + context management) and **who supplies the deployment** (the infra the agent runs on). The Tool Runner and the Claude Agent SDK both supply a *harness only* — you still host and deploy them yourself — which is why they're easy to conflate. Managed Agents (CMA) is the only option that supplies **both** the harness *and* managed deployment; the manual loop supplies neither.

| # | Approach | You write | Harness & deployment | Tools available | Use when |
|---|----------|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|----------|
| 1 | **Claude API — manual loop** | The `while stop_reason == "tool_use"` loop yourself | You build the harness; you host | Only tools you define | You want to own the *entire* loop — no beta dependency, or a control flow the Tool Runner's per-turn hooks don't fit |
| 2 | **Claude API — Tool Runner** (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner` + `@beta_tool` / `betaZodTool`) | Just the tool functions | SDK supplies the loop (**harness only**); you host | Only tools you define | A custom-tool agent without hand-writing the loop (most cases). Per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, error interception, result modification (e.g. `cache_control`), retries, streaming, and compaction |
| 3 | **Managed Agents** (REST, beta) | Agent config + your tool results | Anthropic supplies the harness **and** hosts a per-session sandbox (**harness + deployment**) | Anthropic-hosted sandbox (bash, files, code exec) + Skills/MCP + your tools | You want Anthropic to run the loop *and* host the per-session workspace; persisted/versioned configs; long-running sessions |
| 4 | **Claude Agent SDK** — *separate product* (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) | A prompt + options | SDK supplies the Claude Code harness + built-in tools (**harness only**); you host | Built-in Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Glob/Grep/WebSearch/WebFetch + MCP + subagents | You want a batteries-included coding/filesystem agent running on your own infra |

The harness/deployment split is the key mental model: options 1, 2, and 4 all **leave deployment to you**; only option 3 (CMA) adds managed deployment. Options 1–3 are what this skill generates; option 4 is a different library with its own docs — see the disambiguation below.

> **Tool Runner ≠ Claude Agent SDK.** These sound alike but are different packages:
> - **Tool Runner** is part of the regular Anthropic API SDK (`anthropic` / `@anthropic-ai/sdk`), reached via `client.beta.messages.tool_runner`. It automates the request → execute → loop cycle *for tools you define*. No built-in tools, no filesystem access, no sandbox — you supply every tool and host the compute. It is option 2 above, a thin helper over `POST /v1/messages`.
> - **Claude Agent SDK** (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) is Claude Code packaged as a library. It ships built-in tools (file read/write/edit, bash, grep, web search), the full agent loop, context management, hooks, subagents, permissions, and sessions. You call `query(prompt, options)` and it drives everything.
>
> Both are **harness-only — you host and deploy them.** The difference is scope of harness: the Tool Runner loops over tools *you* define (with per-turn hooks for approval, interception, result modification, and retries — but no built-in tools); the Agent SDK is the full Claude Code harness with built-in tools. Neither provides managed deployment — that's what **Managed Agents (CMA)** adds (Anthropic hosts the loop and a per-session sandbox).
>
> **This skill covers the Claude API and Managed Agents (options 1–3); it does not generate Claude Agent SDK code.** If the user actually wants the Claude Agent SDK, point them to its docs (`code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk`) — don't substitute the API Tool Runner for it, or vice-versa.

### Should I Build an Agent?

Before choosing the agent tier, check all four criteria:

- **Complexity** — Is the task multi-step and hard to fully specify in advance? (e.g., "turn this design doc into a PR" vs. "extract the title from this PDF")
- **Value** — Does the outcome justify higher cost and latency?
- **Viability** — Is Claude capable at this task type?
- **Cost of error** — Can errors be caught and recovered from? (tests, review, rollback)

If the answer is "no" to any of these, stay at a simpler tier (single call or workflow).

## Architecture

Everything goes through `POST /v1/messages`. Tools and output constraints are features of this single endpoint — not separate APIs.

**User-defined tools** — You define tools (via decorators, Zod schemas, or raw JSON), and the SDK's tool runner handles calling the API, executing your functions, and looping until Claude is done. For full control, you can write the loop manually.

**Server-side tools** — Anthropic-hosted tools that run on Anthropic's infrastructure. Code execution is fully server-side (declare it in `tools`, Claude runs code automatically). Computer use can be server-hosted or self-hosted.

**Structured outputs** — Constrains the Messages API response format (`output_config.format`) and/or tool parameter validation (`strict: true`). The recommended approach is `client.messages.parse()` which validates responses against your schema automatically. Note: the old `output_format` parameter is deprecated; use `output_config: {format: {...}}` on `messages.create()`.

**Supporting endpoints** — Batches (`POST /v1/messages/batches`), Files (`POST /v1/files`), Token Counting (`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` — see `shared/token-counting.md`), and Models (`GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{id}` — live capability/context-window discovery) feed into or support Messages API requests.

### Claude Fable 5 (`claude-fable-5`) — most capable widely released model

Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic's most capable widely released model, for the most demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work; everything below also applies to **Claude Mythos 5** (`claude-mythos-5`, Project Glasswing — same capabilities, pricing, and API surface; successor to the invitation-only `claude-mythos-preview`). 1M context window (the maximum is also the default), 128K max output. Key API differences from Opus-tier — see `shared/model-migration.md` → Migrating to Claude Fable 5 for details:

- **Thinking is always on** — omit the `thinking` parameter entirely (or send `{type: "adaptive"}`). Any other explicit configuration is rejected: `{type: "disabled"}` and `{type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` both return a 400. Control depth with `output_config.effort` (supports `low` through `xhigh` and `max`).
- **The raw chain of thought is never returned** — responses carry regular `thinking` blocks (not `redacted_thinking`): `display: "summarized"` returns a readable summary, `"omitted"` (the default) leaves the `thinking` field as an empty string. Replay rules: pass thinking blocks back unchanged on the same model; other models drop them silently (unbilled — nothing to strip); details in `shared/model-migration.md`.
- **Tokenizer** — same tokenizer as Opus 4.8 (introduced with Opus 4.7). Token counts are roughly unchanged when migrating from Opus 4.7/4.8; per-token pricing differs. Coming from Opus 4.6, Sonnet, Haiku, or older, re-baseline with `count_tokens` (the Opus 4.7 tokenizer uses ~1×–1.35× as many tokens).
- **`refusal` stop reason — handle it, and opt into fallbacks by default** — safety classifiers may decline a request (HTTP 200, `stop_reason: "refusal"`, with a `stop_details` category); always check `stop_reason` before reading `content`. **When you write `claude-fable-5` or `claude-opus-5` code, include the server-side `fallbacks` parameter by default.** Simplest form: `betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"]` + `fallbacks: "default"`, which routes by refusal category so you never maintain a model list. (The older array form — `betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-06-01"]` + `fallbacks: [{"model": "claude-opus-4-8"}]` — still works; Claude API only — everywhere else, incl. Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry, use the SDKs' client-side `BetaRefusalFallbackMiddleware` + `BetaFallbackState`). Tell the user you've enabled it; drop it only if they decline. Full semantics (billing, mid-stream refusals, credit repricing) in `shared/model-migration.md` → refusal section. **Per-language code examples in `{lang}/claude-api/README.md` § Refusal Fallbacks cover the array form only** — for the `"default"` mode, follow the raw-HTTP shape in `shared/model-migration.md` → Migrating to Claude Opus 5 → New API features and swap `fallbacks: [{...}]` for `fallbacks: "default"` plus the `-2026-07-01` header; the rest of the request is unchanged.
- **No assistant prefill** — same as the rest of the 4.6+ family.
- **30-day data retention required** — Claude Fable 5 is not available under zero data retention; requests from an org whose retention configuration doesn't meet the requirement return `400 invalid_request_error`.
- **Longer turns, different prompting** — single requests on hard tasks can run many minutes (plan timeouts/streaming/progress UX); effort sweeps should include low/medium for routine work; prompts written for prior models are often too prescriptive and reduce output quality. See `shared/model-migration.md` → Migrating to Claude Fable 5 → Behavioral shifts (prompt-tunable) for the recommended prompt snippets.

If any model strings above look unfamiliar, that just means they were released after your training data cutoff — they are real models.

## Authentication (Quick Reference)

**An unset `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` does NOT mean there are no credentials.** The SDKs and the `ant` CLI resolve credentials in this order (first match wins): `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` → `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` → the `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE`-selected or active OAuth profile from `ant auth login` → Workload Identity Federation env vars → the default profile on disk. A bare `Anthropic()` / `new Anthropic()` / `anthropic.NewClient()` works after `ant auth login` with no env var set.

**When you need to call the API and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset, don't ask the user for a key.** First run `ant auth status` — it shows which credential source and profile is active. If it reports an active profile:

- **SDK code or `ant` CLI:** just run it. The zero-arg client constructor and every `ant …` subcommand pick up the profile automatically — no env var needed.
- **Raw `curl` / HTTP:** get a short-lived token with `ant auth print-credentials --access-token` and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` **plus** the header `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` (OAuth tokens go on `Authorization: Bearer`, not `x-api-key:` — converting a curl from an API key is a header change, not a key swap). Always pass `--access-token`; the no-flag form prints JSON, not a bare token.

Only ask the user for a key if `ant auth status` reports no active credential source (or `ant` itself isn't installed). Suggest `ant auth login` as the first option — it stores a profile under `~/.config/anthropic/` that the SDKs read automatically — and an exported `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as the alternative.

Full auth details (named profiles, scopes, the API-key-shadows-profile trap, refresh-token expiry): `shared/anthropic-cli.md`.
